title: Can this check even fail?

job.text: You asked the AI to summarize an order, and you want to be sure the summary includes the price. Three ways to ask it to check its own work are offered. Pick the one request that would actually catch a summary with no price.

preview.text: The planted summary to catch: "Thanks for your order!" — no price at all.
preview.more: run it against the garbage summary

naivePrompt: Check that the summary includes the price.
basePrompt: Check that the summary includes the price.

text.plain: Check that the summary isn't blank.
Check that the summary is text.
Check that the summary contains a number labeled 'price'.

rules.claim: On the garbage summary: FAIL. On a real summary with a price: PASS.
rules.feedback: This one can say no. It fails the summary with no price and passes one that has it. That's the whole job of a check — to go red on a bad answer.
rules.lesson: A real check references the thing that matters, so it can fail.

output.source: a check that looks at the price

rules.feedback: That check can't fail here. "Thanks for your order!" isn't blank, so this passes it — and it has no price. A check that says yes to garbage checks nothing.

output.source: a check that never says no

rules.feedback: Still green on garbage. "Is it text?" is true of every reply, good or bad. It never says no.
rules.lesson: A check that's always true is vacuous.

output.source: a check that never says no

rules.feedback: Pick a check request. You want the one that goes red on "Thanks for your order!" and green on a summary that has a price. Hit "try to break it" to watch which ones stay green on garbage.
rules.lesson: A real check says no to a bad answer.

hints.nudge: A good check says NO to a bad answer. Which of these ever says no?
hints.gap: Watch "isn't blank" and "is text" both pass "Thanks for your order!" — neither looks at the price.
hints.moves: Only the price check looks at the thing you actually care about (a labeled price), so it's the only one that can fail. Pick Check for a labeled price; leave the other two off.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "check it includes the price" → the AI says "looks good" at garbage.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: ask for a check that looks for a labeled price → the one that can go red.

template.plain: Write me a check for this that would FAIL a bad answer. Then show me it failing a bad example — if it can't fail, it isn't a check.
template.tech: Write an assertion that returns False on a bad output. Run it on an obviously-bad example first and show me it fails; if it stays green, it isn't a check.

notes: ChatGPT: ask it to run the check on an obviously-bad input first; if it stays green, reject it.
Copilot in Excel: a check formula should return FALSE on a bad row — test it on one.
A chat AI that can't run code: ask "what bad answer would this check still pass?" If the answer is "lots", the check is too loose. Never accept "I checked, it's fine."
